title: Diamonds aren’t forever: graphite is carbon’s more stable form
body: At everyday temperature and pressure, graphite, the stuff in pencils, is the most stable arrangement of carbon atoms. Diamond is only metastable: in principle it “wants” to turn into graphite, but its atoms are locked in place by strong bonds and a high energy barrier, so the change would take millions to billions of years. Diamonds are not indestructible, though; in pure oxygen they ignite at roughly 690 to 840 °C and burn away to carbon dioxide.

slides.question: If graphite is more stable, why don’t diamonds turn into graphite?
options: A high energy barrier locks the atoms
Diamond is really the stabler form
Oxygen in the air protects them
They do, within a few decades
slides.explanation: Diamond is metastable: its atoms are held by strong bonds and a high energy barrier, so the change would take millions to billions of years.

slides.heading: Which one is not a form of carbon?
slides.explanation: Quartz is silicon dioxide. Diamond, graphite and graphene are all pure carbon with the atoms bonded in different patterns; at room conditions graphite is the most stable of them.
